los.text: Name the parts of the developing respiratory tract, identify the processes by which this tract forms and matures, and identify the processes of the formation of all other structures of the respiratory system
los.html:
• Origin: the respiratory diverticulum (lung bud) grows from the ventral foregut in week 4.
TissueGerm layer
Epithelium and glands of larynx, trachea, bronchi, alveoliEndoderm
Cartilage, smooth muscle, connective tissue, vesselsSplanchnic mesoderm
Visceral pleuraSplanchnic mesoderm
Parietal pleuraSomatic mesoderm
Laryngeal cartilages and muscles4th and 6th pharyngeal arches
Tracheo-oesophageal septum
  • Separates the trachea from the oesophagus.
  • Failure → oesophageal atresia ± tracheo-oesophageal fistula (commonest: blind upper oesophagus with a fistula to the lower part): polyhydramnios
  • Frothy saliva
  • Choking on feeds
  • NG tube won't pass
  • Part of VACTERL.
Branching
  • Lung bud
  • → 2 bronchial buds (week 5)
  • → 3 right and 2 left lobar bronchi
  • → segmental bronchi (week 7)
  • → ~23 generations.
StageWeeksEvents
Embryonic4–7Lung bud, lobar and segmental bronchi
Pseudoglandular5–17Branching to the terminal bronchioles; no gas exchange possible
Canalicular16–25Respiratory bronchioles, capillaries grow in, type I and II cells appear; survival possible from ~24 weeks
Saccular24–birthTerminal sacs; surfactant rises
Alveolar~36 weeks–8 yearsMature alveoli; most form after birth
  • Surfactant: made by type II pneumocytes from ~20–24 weeks
    • enough by ~34–35 weeks.
    • Lack → neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (preterm, maternal diabetes delays it).
    • Antenatal corticosteroids speed up maturation.
  • Lung growth needs fetal breathing movements, amniotic fluid and room in the chest:
CauseResult
Oligohydramnios (renal agenesis, ruptured membranes)Pulmonary hypoplasia
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (left posterolateral, Bochdalek; pleuroperitoneal membrane fails)Gut in the chest → pulmonary hypoplasia
  • Diaphragm forms from 4 parts: septum transversum (central tendon), pleuroperitoneal membranes, oesophageal mesentery (crura), body wall muscle.
  • It starts in the neck, so it keeps its C3–5 (phrenic) supply.
Pleural cavitiesFrom the intraembryonic coelom, separated from the pericardial cavity by pleuropericardial membranes and from the peritoneal cavity by the pleuroperitoneal membranes.
At birthLung fluid is squeezed out and absorbed, air fills the alveoli, pulmonary vascular resistance falls and pulmonary blood flow rises.
